findings.title: Denial-cache key omits identity type, causing cross-identity false denies
findings.body: In Service.Check the denial key is built as userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent) with no identity type. Anonymous subject 'anonymous:0' and renderer subject 'render:0' both resolve to UID '0', and user vs service-account UIDs can also collide as strings. A denial cached for one identity type (e.g. anonymous denied dashboards:read on dash1) will therefore hit for a different identity type on the same namespace/action/resource (e.g. renderer, which is allowed dashboards:read/folders:read) and Check returns Allowed:false without consulting permissions. The fix is to include IdentityType in the denial key.

findings.title: Negative caching reintroduces stale denies for newly granted access
findings.body: Service.Check caches every deny in permDenialCache for shortCacheTTL (30s) and short-circuits future Checks on a hit before reading permissions. If a user is denied and then granted access to the same dashboard/folder (the exact creator flow this PR fixes, role/team/assignment change, or folder-tree refresh), subsequent Checks within the TTL incorrectly return denied without hitting the DB. The fast deny path defeats the new fallback-to-DB logic for the most important transition from deny to allow.

findings.title: Every cached deny now forces a full DB permission fetch
findings.body: Check first reads getCachedIdentityPermissions and, if the cached scope map does not contain the resource, unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions. The cache-hit fast paths were removed from getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions, so that call always queries basic roles, teams and permissions from the DB. Previously a fresh permCache hit decided allow/deny without I/O. Now any user without access to a resource hits the DB on first Check per resource, and scanning N distinct denied resources causes N DB permission builds (only the second identical-resource hit is absorbed by the denial cache). This turns deny-heavy workloads into a DB storm.

findings.title: List still serves stale cached permissions with no DB fallback
findings.body: Check was changed to fall back to the DB when cached permissions do not contain the requested resource, but List was changed to use getCachedIdentityPermissions with no equivalent fallback: on a permCache hit it directly calls listPermission. A newly granted dashboard/folder will therefore be missing from List results for up to shortCacheTTL while Check already allows it, leaving Check and List inconsistent and the creator flow still broken for listings.

findings.title: Denial-precedence test stores false instead of true
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' seeds permCache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} and claims this proves the denial entry is checked instead of the allow. Since checkPermission treats a false map value the same as missing (it tests truthiness), both caches deny. The test never exercises denial-wins-over-allow. It should seed map value true, otherwise a regression that ignores permDenialCache would still pass.
